fixes.explanation: The verse says there was no one. It describes a people who “…have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say…” the words “Send them back!” This is a heavy verse. Nobody steps up in it.

False is right, and it's a hard verse. They “…have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say…” the words “Send them back!” Nobody speaks up for them here. I think that's the heaviest part.
Right out to the far edge of the map, friend. The verse says, “…His praise from the ends of the earth…” (Isaiah 42:10). The call goes way past one building.

Mountaintops, friend. The verse says, “Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them cry out from the mountaintops.” Sela is a city in Edom (2 Kings 14:7). A mountaintop is a spot where your voice carries.

Gates are a fine spot for shouting news, but that's not what this verse says. It says Sela's people are to “…cry out from the mountaintops.” I'd be winded before I got to the top, and I'd sing the first line at about half volume.
False is right. God says, “I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.” No flood in this verse. The rivers become dry land, and the marshes are drained (Isaiah 42:15).

Light goes in the first blank. God says, “I will turn darkness into light before them…” (Isaiah 42:16). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and the light is a very big deal to me. He's doing this for the blind He leads.
That's the verse. God says those who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ “will be turned back in utter shame.” That's how it ends for them, according to God.
The islands are part of the song, but this verse says nothing about a welcome for them. It says those who trust in idols “will be turned back in utter shame.” Turned back, and ashamed.
That's the twist, friend. God asks, “Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I am sending?” He's pointing at His own servant. I did not see that coming.
Hear is the word. God says, “Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear.” The ears are open, but the hearing isn't happening.
Obey is the word. The passage asks, “Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?” Hearing is the first step, and obeying comes with it.

Leaving would be a quick way out, but that's not what the verse asks. It asks, “Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?” The blank is obey, and the question is about who will listen.

Yes, friend, and it's a hard one. The passage asks, “Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned?” The way the question is put points straight to the LORD.
